An '''atlatl,''' '''energy ball atlatl''' or '''Gungan atlatl''' was a [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] throwing stick used to launch [[Booma/Legends|energy balls]] a longer distance than the naked arm could achieve. The ball's outer layer broke on impact, releasing a plasma and electric shock that damaged the target. Atlatls were sometimes used as blunt force weapons. Atlatls were carved from a naturally isolating wood, so that the wielder would not be affected should the ball break while on the atlatl. As such, the wielder could use the atlatl as a club in melee combat, breaking the ball on contact with an enemy. The atlatl had a shorter range than other similar Gungan tools to throw energy balls, like the [[Cesta/Legends|cesta]], but it was much more precise and, being a one-handed weapon, allowed the warrior to hold an [[Gungan personal energy shield/Legends|energy shield]] for protection in the other hand. In addition, atlatls could be used to fish.

[[Militiagung/Legends|Militiagungs]] in the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] were trained in the use of atlatl in the times before [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], even though the Gungans had spent many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] without a war. When the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] threatened the Gungan civilization in 32 BBY, the Gungan Grand Army used atlatls and other traditional weapons in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Grassy Plains]]. Years later, [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] used an atlatl to teach fishing skills to his child, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].

==Description==
The atlatl,<ref name="FF11">{{FactFile|11|GUN 1-2|Gungan Weapons}}</ref> energy ball atlatl<ref name="TOY1">[[Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|''Star Wars: Episode I'' toy line]]</ref> or Gungan atlatl<ref name="encA">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' (atlatl, Gungan)</ref> was a non-conductive hardwood utensil naturally shaped as a short throwing stick with a cradle in one of its ends.<ref name="NEGW" /> While the item itself was organic, growing naturally as a single piece with its peculiar shape,<ref name="FF11" /> it was still carved out of the trees growing on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="NEGW" /> Those woods had natural isolating properties that the atlatl kept.<ref name="FF11" /> Traditionally, the owner fashioned an atlatl with personal motifs.<ref name="NEGW" /> A finished, ready-for-use atlatl weighed 1.5 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="CORE" />

[[File:AtlAtlBooma-FFp39.png|thumb|left|150px|An atlatl loaded with a booma]]
The atlatl was a traditional weapon for the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="CORE" /> Gungans used grenade-like projectiles known as [[Booma/Legends|energy balls]],<ref name="NEGW" /><ref name="FF11" /><ref name="TOYP">''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]''</ref> booma<ref name="FF11" /> or boomers,<ref name="TOYP" /> that were thrown against a target. Breaking the shell on impact, the booma released a liquid-like plasma and an electric shock that damaged both organic and technological targets.<ref name="NEGW" /><ref name="FF11" /> The shape of the atlatl was optimal to place on its cradle one&mdash;and only one&mdash;energy ball of the right size,<ref name="NEGW" /><ref name="TOYP" /> a small energy ball.<ref name="encA" /> Then, an individual&mdash;commonly a Gungan&mdash;could launch the ball from the atlatl,<ref name="TPM" /><ref name="E1IG">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref><ref name="E1VD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> with a longer range than the naked arm would achieve.<ref name="CORE" /><ref name="FF11" />

The specific length of the atlatl handle provided the additional strength and speed, and the cradle released the ball at the apex of the throw.<ref name="FF11" /> With a maximum range of 100 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], and an optimal range of 30 meters, the atlatl was very precise in short distances,<ref name="NEGW" /> and it could be used with only one hand.<ref name="SON" /><ref name="TPM" /><ref name="encA" />

Being a throwing stick,<ref name="CORE" /><ref name="encA" /> it could also be used as a simple club in melee combat<ref name="CORE" /> should the user feel cornered<ref name="NEGW" /> or in a desperate situation.<ref name="encA" /> If the atlatl was holding an energy ball and the wielder used the atlatl as a club, the energy ball would explode when hitting the target, but the isolating material of the atlatl would protect the wielder from any harmful effect. For the same reason, the wielder would also be protected should the energy ball accidentally explode while still on the atlatl.<ref name="FF11" />

Gungan weapon technology had different tools to throw energy balls, at varying range and precision.<ref name="TPM" /><ref name="encE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' (Energy ball)</ref> The Gungan catapult had a much greater range than the atlatl and used much bigger energy balls, but it had a much slower firing rate.<ref name="FF11" /> The [[Cesta/Legends|cesta]], a longer, staff-like version of the atlatl,<ref name="NEGW" /> had a greater range<ref name="CORE" /><ref name="encA" /> but was far less precise<ref name="NEGW" /><ref name="CORE" /><ref name="encA" /> and required two hands to manipulate.<ref name="NEGW" /> As the atlatl was more compact than a cesta, a warrior could wield an atlatl in one hand and protect him- or herself with a [[Gungan personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shield]] in the other hand.<ref name="NEGW" /><ref name="SON" /> When not using it, the warrior could attach the atlatl to the belt or the backpack,<ref name="NEGW" /> with the latter being preferred for easier transport.<ref name="SON" />

Another version of the atlatl, the [[Pocker LJ]], could be used to fish. The fisherman aimed with a [[laser sighting unit]] that adjusted automatically for the refraction in the water, then prepared a projectile. By turning the handle, a barely visible but very strong line was formed between the fisherman and its fish. The fish could be outright killed while still in the water, or it could be hit in certain areas to leave it defenseless.<ref name="AOTCn">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>

==History==
The Gungan sentient species, evolved on the planet Naboo, had a military tradition to adopt organic technology to protect its submarine civilization.<ref name="GWDB">{{DB|technology|gunganweaponry|Gungan weaponry}}</ref> Through the history of the Army, Gungan foot soldiers were known to carry atlatls, cestas, [[Electropole/Legends|electropoles]],<ref name="encG">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' (Gungan)</ref><ref name="EGwarf">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and some other cultural weapons, with battle wagons being used to carry the energy balls.<ref name="EGwarf" />

[[File:Gungan_warrior.png|thumb|right|250px|An [[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]] Gungan armed with an atlatl and [[Booma/Legends|boomas]]]]
By [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], the Gungans had not had a war in many years, but they still kept a professional [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] mostly for ornamental purposes, and for protection against natural, aquatic predators.<ref name="GWDB" /> At that point, in the city of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], the [[Otoh Gunga Defense League/Legends|Otoh Gunga Defense League]]<ref name="NEGW" /> built the so-called Otoh Gunga standard-issue atlatl to be used by the Grand Army. Gungans in the army were trained to use atlatl and cesta in ranged and melee combat. Rumor said that Otoh Gunga had warehouses with enough supplies to provide one atlatl to each of the soldiers&mdash;or "Militiagungs"&mdash;in the Army.<ref name="SON" />

Around that time, most Gungan warriors carried atlatl and cestas in their patrols. [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]] was known to carry several traditional Gungan weapons,<ref name="E1IG" /> including a cesta and an electropole.<ref name="CTDB">{{DB|character|captaintarpals|Tarpals, Captain}}</ref> [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Mokem (researcher)|Mokem]], whose five-Gungan cavalry patrol protected [[Lianorm Swamp/Legends|Lianorm Swamp]] from strangers, carried with him a cesta, an atlatl and an energy shield, while each of his subordinates had to choose between a cesta or an atlatl.<ref name="PON">{{WizCite|story=Peril on Naboo|book=Secrets of Naboo}}</ref> Non-military Gungans also had access to atlatls: Several Gungan mystics that ministered the people of Otoh Gunga had atlatls as their weapons of choice.<ref name="CORE" />

In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], when the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invaded]] Naboo and captured the [[Human/Legends|Human]] cities, the Gungans patrolled their swamps with their atlatls and cestas ready.<ref name="PON" /> Soon afterward, the Gungans allied with the Naboo against the Federation. The Gungan Grand Army gathered in the plains [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|to fight]] the Federation army, mostly composed of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]]. Several Gungan [[Officer/Legends|officers]], including Captain Tarpals<ref name="CTDB" /> and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], were armed with atlatls,<ref name="TOY1" /> as were many of the soldiers.<ref name="TPM" /> The atlatl's quick firing rate was useless in the conflict due to the weapon's short range.<ref name="FF11" /> The battle ended when the droid army was unilaterally deactivated.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

[[File:GunganBattleDroid-BTCG.png|thumb|left|250px|A Gungan warrior prepares to use a booma-laden atlatl on a B1 battle droid]]
Later, Gungan General [[Ceel]] built a [[Scrumma Jawbone training center|training center]] on [[Scrumma Jawbone]], an arm of [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]], for the Militiagungs to train in the use of atlatl, cesta and other Gungan weapons. The center used floating bull's-eyes, bobbing targets and methane gasbags; it was avoided by the local fauna.<ref name="NEGW" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] trained his [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in the use of ion-burst-powered atlatl for fishing purposes on the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="AOTCn" />

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Gungan Grand Army was sent to help the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and its allies on [[Dac/Legends|Dac]]. The Militiagungs used atlatls and other traditional arms in their attack, with the atlatls being effective against the Confederacy-aligned [[Bioweapon/Legends|bioweapons]] called [[Hydroid Medusa/Legends|Hydroid Medusas]].<ref name="Gungan Attack">{{TCW|Gungan Attack}}</ref>

Soon afterward, the Gungans allied with the Confederacy and the Militiagungs readied their atlatls and other weapons to attack the Human city [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] on Naboo along with Confederacy battle droids. Just before the battle, the Gungan leadership, having discovered foul play, decided to oppose the Confederacy instead: The Militiagungs deactivated the droids and then attacked the Confederacy commander, General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], using their atlatls as ranged weapons. The atlatls successfully damaged Grievous' [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] body and, along with other attacks, helped in Grievous' eventual capture during the skirmish.<ref name="Shadow Warrior">{{TCW|Shadow Warrior}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The atlatl first appeared in the movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] ([[1999]]) as an unnamed prop used by computer-generated Gungan soldiers. The action figure of "[[Kaadu/Legends|Kaadu]] and Jar Jar Binks" creature set (1999) included a representation of the atlatl that was identified as "Energy Ball Atlatl," giving a name to the item. The later figure "Captain Tarpals & Kaadu" from the ''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]'' series ([[2001]]), also featuring the item, called it "Atlatl with Energy Ball Hand-Held Weapon."<ref name="scum">{{Rebelscum|url=potj12kaadu.asp|text=Rebelscum review of the figure}}</ref>

A real-life [[Wikipedia:Atlatl|atlatl]] is a tool used for throwing spears farther. This tool has been in existence for over 25,000 years.<ref name="spear">{{WebCite|url=http://www.worldatlatl.org/WhatisAtlatl.html|text=the World Atlatl Association|archivedate=20060616133611}}</ref>

[[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]] featured the atlatl with [[roleplaying game]] stats in both ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]'' ([[2000]]) and the later ''[[Secrets of Naboo]]'' (2001), but with inconsistencies between the versions: ''Core Rulebook'' values the item at 50 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and considers that the club's damage was of two four-sided dice, or two eight-sided dice when throwing an energy ball.<ref name="CORE" /> ''Secrets of Naboo'' specifically says that atlatls are not sold, reduces its melee damage to one six-sided die and increases its ranged damage to two eight-sided dice plus two,<ref name="SON" /> even though fixed modifiers to the damage ("plus two") were supposedly applied only to melee attacks.<ref name="CORE" />

The video game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' features Gungan soldiers using unidentified traditional weapons that might or might not be atlatls. If they could be identified as such, then that would mean that atlatls were in use as early as [[3000 BBY]].<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref><ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>
